newsitem.title: USA: National TechTeam sees Q2 at breakeven.
newsitem.headline: National TechTeam sees Q2 at breakeven.

text.p: National TechTeam Inc said its second quarter earnings will be below analysts' expectations and should be breakeven with a year ago.

In a press release, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer William Coyro said second quarter performance will be down because of project delays in the first half of 1997 for the firm's call center services and significant start up costs from a number of new contracts.
The company said it plans to release second quarter results August 1.

The company's stock had been halted for news pending. It was down four at 11-7/8. The most recent analysts' consensus for the second quarter was $0.14 a share, versus $0.09 a year ago, according to First Call Corp.
Coyro said the company expects to have a strong second half because of a number of major new contracts that include TechTeam's existing accounts and several new customers.

He said the company expects to announce a number of new contracts in the second half of the year. Coyro said TechTeam has expensed a large amount of infrastructure, development, sales and marketing costs related to the contracts in the second quarter.

"TechTeam is in a very strong position with regard both to the quantity and quality of new business that it has today," he said. "Demand for TechTeam's services continues to be strong and we believe the call center and corporate computer service industries will continue to grow worldwide."
The company said in a statement the recent stock price drop has "no correlation" to its strong financial position.
